strengths: EA-KD offers a simple, practical modification: teacher and student entropies determine per-sample distillation weights without an auxiliary network. Its compatibility with both logit and feature distillation is useful for computer vision.

The experimental breadth is substantial. Table 2 reports improvements in 46 of 49 CIFAR-100 comparisons, averaging 0.56 percentage points. Gains over vanilla KD include 3.39 points on Tiny-ImageNet, 0.76 on ImageNet, and 0.81–1.68 AP on COCO. Transformer-to-CNN and language-model experiments provide additional evidence of applicability.

The paper includes component and temperature ablations, a DKD hyperparameter study, timing measurements, and supplementary comparisons with TTM/WTTM. Repeated-run statistics, citations to datasets and baseline methods, and a public code link support the empirical presentation.
weaknesses: The experiments do not adequately separate sample prioritization from changing overall distillation strength. Equation (12) uses weights without mean normalization, altering the effective balance between distillation and supervised losses. The entropy, inverse-entropy, and component ablations also change this scale. The MLD+LS coefficient adjustment from 9 to 4 reinforces this concern. Tuned constant-weight baselines and mean-normalized weighting controls are needed to attribute gains to the proposed adaptive mechanism.

The incremental contribution over existing uncertainty-based weighting is modest and incompletely established. WTTM already emphasizes uncertain teacher predictions. In Table 9, teacher-only weighting accounts for most improvements and exceeds the combined factor for FCFD. Table A1 shows only 0.03–0.19 percentage-point improvements over WTTM, small relative to reported variability. These results provide limited support for the claimed superiority of student-dependent adaptation.

The theoretical interpretation overreaches the analysis. With a uniform student, KL divergence equals log(C) minus teacher entropy; a nearly uniform teacher has low loss because its output already resembles the student's. Equations (5)–(7) therefore do not establish harmful neglect of useful knowledge. Predictive entropy need not measure learning value, and t-SNE proximity does not establish classifier decision boundaries. The analogous claim about feature MSE is also insufficiently substantiated.

Uncertainty reporting is incomplete for the closest comparisons. Appendix C gives standard deviations for EA variants without corresponding baseline variability. This limits confidence in small improvements such as the 0.16-point average gain over MLD+LS and the 0.11 AP gain over DKD on COCO, although the larger vanilla-KD gains remain persuasive.

Important implementation choices remain unclear: whether gradients propagate through student entropy, and how weights are aggregated and applied to detection regions and language-model sequences. Differentiating through the weights introduces an additional gradient term, making this consequential for reproducing and interpreting the method.
